bug_semantics: Legacy PyTorch serialization unpickles the first pickle to obtain MAGIC_NUMBER, so that value may be computed by a REDUCE callable rather than encoded as an INT/LONG opcode. picklescan's get_magic_number instead disassembled the first pickle and returned only the first opcode whose name contained INT or LONG. An attacker could encode eval('0x1950A86A20F9469CFC6C') as the first pickle: PyTorch obtains the correct magic number, while picklescan obtains None and rejects/abandons the PyTorch scan before examining the later pickle containing the dangerous payload. The file therefore remains loadable by PyTorch while the scanner misses the code-execution globals.
flaw_origin: Commit f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 introduced old-format PyTorch scanning and, in the same focused commit, created src/picklescan/torch.py:get_magic_number with the literal INT/LONG-opcode heuristic and src/picklescan/scanner.py:scan_pytorch with the pre-scan magic-number rejection. Its immediate parent had neither torch.py nor scan_pytorch, so this is the smallest original commit that wrote the flawed semantic approximation; later cursor, exception-handling, routing, and logging changes retained rather than originated it.
ai_marker: absent: `git cat-file -p f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9` shows human author and committer `Luc Georges <luc@huggingface.co>`, subject `feat: add pytorch old format support`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, bot, or other trailer/identity marker in the BIC commit object.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/mmaitre314/picklescan/security/advisories/GHSA-97f8-7cmv-76j2 describes the mismatch: get_magic_number uses pickletools.genops and accepts INT/LONG, whereas PyTorch uses pickle_module.load; its PoC places eval('MAGIC_NUMBER') in __reduce__, causing picklescan to report an invalid magic number and scan zero files while torch.load proceeds to the malicious payload. The advisory declares affected versions <1.0.3 and patched version 1.0.3.

A targeted standard-library reproduction of the first pickle produced opcodes PROTO, GLOBAL, BINPUT, BINUNICODE, BINPUT, TUPLE1, BINPUT, REDUCE, BINPUT, STOP. Applying the historical `"INT" in opcode.name or "LONG" in opcode.name` extraction returned None, while pickle.loads returned 119547037146038801333356, exactly 0x1950A86A20F9469CFC6C. This directly confirms the advisory's semantic mismatch without executing the later malicious payload.

`git log -p -L :get_magic_number:src/picklescan/torch.py b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c^` traces the literal opcode loop to f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9. Later commits 5246bdfc94fb5f169e04aac80b1a0559ab381692 (cursor reset) and c4748bcabe795b4e8f3e3b3174683e3bcc21b92b (ValueError handling) retained the same literal-only decision.

`git log -p -L :scan_pytorch:src/picklescan/scanner.py b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c^` independently traces `magic = get_magic_number(data)` followed by `if magic != MAGIC_NUMBER: raise InvalidMagicError(...)` to the same f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 commit. Commit 648485cf84f9253be2c21ac6ebb6a348a65d86af later converted that rejection into an empty scan-error result at the scan_bytes boundary, and 28a7b4ef753466572bda3313737116eeb9b4e5c5 later added a generic-pickle fallback there, but neither changed the vulnerable direct scan_pytorch/get_magic_number contract.

`git show f98f9bd8 -- src/picklescan/scanner.py src/picklescan/torch.py` shows one focused non-merge commit creating all 75 lines of torch.py, including get_magic_number, and adding scan_pytorch plus .pt/.pth/.ckpt/.bin routing. `git rev-parse f98f9bd8^` resolves the sole immediate parent to 72aa7c432bc59819d07393bf91623fa963896ebe; `git cat-file -e 72aa7c432bc59819d07393bf91623fa963896ebe:src/picklescan/torch.py` fails because the path is absent, and the parent-to-BIC patch adds scan_pytorch from zero lines. This directly verifies parent absence and rules out a move/refactor/squash aggregate.

Release-history checks place the BIC before the vulnerable release range: `git tag --contains f98f9bd8 --sort=version:refname` includes v0.0.3 and every subsequent release through v1.0.2 but excludes the pre-BIC v0.0.2. The release timeline dates v0.0.2 before the BIC and v0.0.3 after it, establishing v0.0.3 as the first tagged release containing the flawed old-format scanner.

The advisory-linked fix b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c directly changes src/picklescan/scanner.py:scan_pytorch: on an absent/mismatched literal magic it seeks to byte zero, scans the first pickle for globals, merges dangerous globals when present, then scans the following five pickles rather than abandoning the file. The same commit adds a regression payload/test and bumps setup.cfg from 1.0.2 to 1.0.3.

The patched boundary is exact: `git rev-parse b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c^` is 9f8b998c3b119037d97029d4ee4dc45ae4a439b0, identical to `v1.0.2^{}`; `git tag --points-at b9997634683a4f4bd0c7e3701e7ce7e90fe70e8c` returns v1.0.3. Thus the vulnerable parent is the last affected tag and the direct fix is the first patched tag.

BIC-only AI inspection used the raw commit object, not PR text or later commits: f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 has one parent, author and committer Luc Georges <luc@huggingface.co>, a one-line human-authored feature subject, and no trailers or bot/AI identity.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins with the old-format PyTorch feature itself. PyTorch establishes format validity by unpickling its first object, but the new picklescan implementation substituted a syntactic search for a literal integer opcode and rejected the file before scanning payload pickles when that search failed. The immediate parent lacks both the helper file and the old-format scan function, while the BIC adds the complete flawed mechanism in one ordinary, single-parent commit, making f98f9bd89b16ab1b1b1b6366acddd1b2a4d36fe9 smaller and more causal than subsequent error-handling or routing commits. The dynamic-REDUCE reproduction demonstrates that a valid PyTorch magic value can have no INT/LONG opcode, and the advisory demonstrates how a dangerous later pickle is consequently skipped. Tag containment puts the flaw in releases beginning with v0.0.3 and still in v1.0.2. The direct fix is the v1.0.3 tag commit: it treats a nonliteral magic as suspicious, scans and merges the first pickle's globals, and continues through the payload sequence. Finally, the BIC's raw commit object contains only a named human author/committer and no AI marker, so under the required BIC-only attribution rule the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
